epic:#26676#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_cdb7a717def74e719988f089fbaa18ff

The maintainer asked for more testing here: 「继续测试」 (2026-11-04). Measured on `main` `987ff33b88`, CLI and server built from that commit. This widens the card: the install also locks the target out of further customization.

## Result by item type

Source: `os dev`, one `.custom` holding the items below, published and served there. Export: `os package export`. Target: a fresh `os start`, separate database, same base package. Install: `os package install FILE -r TARGET --email OWNER`, which prints `✓ Package installed into the running kernel`.

| Item in the exported file | On the source | On the target after install | After a target restart |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Override, `view` | Served | **Not served**, base label | Not served |
| Override, `dashboard` | Served | **Not served** | Not served |
| Override, `app` | Served | **Not served** | Not served |
| Override, `dataset` | Served | **Not served** | Not served |
| New item, `view` under its own name | Served | Served | Served |

`GET /api/v1/packages/com.example.asset-repair/customizations` answers `overrides: 4` on the source and `overrides: 0` on the target. The exported file does carry all four with their `overrides` block.

## The install also closes the door behind it

| Step on the target, after the install | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `POST /packages/com.example.asset-repair/ensure-customization` | 200, `created: false`, **`writable: false`** |
| Save a view override into the pair, as Studio does | 422 `Cannot create view/… that package is read-only (provided by code or an installed app)` |
| `DELETE /api/v1/packages/com.example.asset-repair.custom` | 422 `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED … it is read-only` |
| `os package install FILE --install-mode unmanaged` | 422 `INSTALL_MODE_NOT_PERMITTED`: the file names no `installModes`, so only `managed` is allowed |

So a customer who follows the documented path ends with no change applied and no way to customize that base on that instance. The only recovery the seat found is deleting the cached file by hand from the host, and restarting.

The same install on a target whose pair already exists and is writable also reports success, and the overrides still do not apply. The seat did not read whether rows already in that pair survive or are shadowed.

## Where the cached file lives

The install wrote `.objectstack/installed-packages/com.example.asset-repair.custom.json` under the server's working directory even though that server ran with `OS_HOME` set elsewhere. A later instance started from the same directory with a different `OS_HOME` and a fresh database picked the package up. This was found by accident, when one test contaminated the next. A container's working directory is usually not on a volume, so whether the install survives a container replacement was not measured.

## Likely cause, from reading the code

- Every read of an override asks `sys_metadata` rows: `listServedOverrides` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-served-overrides.ts` selects `where: { package_id: pair.value, state: 'active' }`.
- The install registers the file's items in the in-memory registry as a code-provided package and writes no such row. The server log shows `[Registry] Registered view: com.example.asset-repair.custom:asset_repair_ticket.open`.

That explains both halves: no row means no override served, and a registered package counts as provided by code, so it is not writable. This is a reading and was not confirmed by a fix.

## Other door tried

`POST /api/v1/packages` does not take the exported file: 400 on the missing `manifest.type`, and with a `type` added, 400 `Unrecognized key(s)… apps, dashboards, datasets, viewItems`. So no other published door was found for carrying a `.custom` between environments.

## Not measured

- Other overridable types: `report`, `translation`, `email_template`, `page`, `doc`, `book`, `mapping`.
- Object extensions (`__c` fields) carried in a `.custom`.
- The Docker path, because Docker is not running on this machine.

## Expected, restated

ADR-0146 D2 says the pair is "exported, committed, reviewed and deployed to another environment as any package is". After the install, the target serves the overrides, the customizations read lists them, and an administrator there can keep customizing. If an item cannot be applied, the install says so and does not print success.

triage#1 · os-zhuang · session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U

Path: none

## Triage: first-touch audit · p1 · `domain:server` · `pm:queue` · 2026-11-04T14:53Z

⛔ Not a claim.

- Read fresh. The documented ADR-0146 D2 path (export a `.custom`, install it on another environment) prints success. But none of its overrides (view, dashboard, app, dataset) is served on the target, and the install leaves the target's pair read-only, so it can be neither customized nor removed. A silent failure of a documented deployment path that also locks the target, so p1.
- Fix site: the package install door and the CLI (`os package install`). Serial with #30062 (declared overrides).
